facts.raw_span: asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules
symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
Face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions had resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL; reference range 50-250/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL; reference range <11.5 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL; reference range 211-911 pg/mL)
Negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
no pathologic findings on CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in upper dermis
FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR
Hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils (20%, reference range <5%)

concepts.why: The patient's hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR are consistent with Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia.
The patient's elevated tryptase and nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in upper dermis are consistent with Mastocytosis.
The patient's hypereosinophilia and increased eosinophils in bone marrow are consistent with Hypereosinophilic Syndrome.
The patient's FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR and hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia are consistent with Myeloproliferative Neoplasm.
The patient's asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules, symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce, are consistent with Eosinophilic Dermatitis.

The patient's hypereosinophilia, nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in upper dermis, and increased eosinophils in bone marrow are consistent with Lymphocytic Variant of Hypereosinophilic Syndrome.
